closes.text: CAUSE: the analyzer marks a binding holding an awaiting closure as async, so calls through it await on both backends, but the native emitter chose the closure's form from its position alone: at a `let`, a `void` closure took the floating form (spawn the body) while the call site still awaited it. RULE: a closure value answers a future natively wherever JavaScript awaits a call through it; anywhere else it floats (JavaScript runs the body to its first suspension; native spawns, and `spawn` polls eagerly, so the order is the same). Covered and pinned on both backends, 17 `b743_*` pins asserting node's exact lines (15 red before the fix): called through a local, module-level, `mut` or `async |T| U` binding; passed to a `|T| void`, an `async |T| void` or a plain `|T| U` parameter (and a synchronous binding passed to an `async` parameter is lifted into a ready future); stored in a field, a list or an `Option`; UI `|| void` handlers; returned. STILL REFUSED by name: an awaiting closure literal that returns a value at a position nothing awaits; an async function named as a value; closures with a view parameter or a `context` clause. SECOND BUG behind the related symptom, on BOTH backends: a trait default was emitted under the async state of whichever function first reached it, so a synchronous caller printed `[object Promise]` on JavaScript and the native build was refused; a default is now emitted under its own state (native `default_instance`, JS `emit_default_instance`); one JS pin in `inference::async_inference`, red before. No corpus golden moved; no program that built before changes its order. The examples' workarounds (`held_text`, `spare_screen`) are gone (2262e8ca), listings byte-identical. Two new internal refusals in `lib.rs`, unreachable behind their guards: `a floating closure value of no closure type`, `a lifted closure value of no closure type`
